Alright, User Flair looks ready to go. Here's an explanation of the CSS to assign flair:

CSS

The CSS uses this image and essentially assigns the flair to the user by moving down the file. This makes the CSS a little slimmer and requires less management of the imgur files (as it is only in there once). I used http://www.retinaspritegenerator.com/ to generate the sprite list.

The CSS is in two parts, part one:

/* Generic Settings for Flair */

a[href="/user/Nofrill"]:not(.upvoatsGiven)::after,

a[href="/user/Thegreatandpowerfulr"]:not(.upvoatsGiven)::after {

display: inline-block;

content: "";

background-repeat: no-repeat;

background-position: left top;

padding: 0px;

margin: 0px;

margin-left: 5px;

background-color: transparent;

vertical-align: middle;

background-image: url("http://i.imgur.com/rE40MSm.png");

height: 20px;

}

For every user we want to assign flair, we need to add them to the beginning section of this CSS code.

As you move down the CSS, you will find the individual CSS for each respective flair. When a flair is not utilized the code just sits there doing nothing as per below:

/*Cross Flair */ {

width: 85px;

background-position: 0 -80px;

}

When we want to assign flair to a specific user, you simply copy and paste the same CSS from the first section of user flair ensuring that a comma separates each user and that the last user has no comma after.

/*Conklin Flair */

a[href="/user/Thegreatandpowerfulr"]:not(.upvoatsGiven)::after {

width: 58px;

background-position: 0 -60px;

}

As you can see the width is set on a per flair basis and the background-position property indicates how far down the sprite file to go!
